analyst_view.overall: Early view: Heerenveen under Robin Veldman are in good form and have one of the league's best defences, with the most clean sheets in the division as of early November and a clean bill of health at that point. Go Ahead Eagles under Joseph Oosting score freely through Soren Tengstedt but have conceded in every league game and had not won away in six. Their goalkeeper Nick Marsman is out until early January, so Jasper Cillessen is expected in goal.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean a little lower: Heerenveen have one of the tightest defences in the league and kept five clean sheets in their first 11 games. Go Ahead should still score through Tengstedt, but a high-scoring game would go against Heerenveen's form at home.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. Nothing in the news points either way: Heerenveen should have more of the ball at home, and Go Ahead play a 4-2-3-1 with wide players like Oskar Sivertsen, which fits the split the numbers already show.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards. No referee has been named yet and there are no suspension or rivalry angles, so I stay with the numbers for now.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots. Heerenveen should create plenty at home with Dylan Vente and Levi Smans, and Go Ahead are an open side, so I see no reason to move away from the numbers yet.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Heerenveen's defence limits good chances, but Go Ahead's open style gives Heerenveen room on the break, so I stay with the numbers.
